name: Rialto Bridge
overview: The Rialto Bridge is one of four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice and the oldest of the four. This iconic stone bridge is lined with shops and is one of Venice's most recognizable landmarks and architectural marvels.
history: The first bridge on this site was a pontoon bridge built in 1181. It was replaced by a wooden bridge in 1255, which collapsed twice. The current stone bridge was designed by Antonio da Ponte and completed in 1591 after much controversy over its design.
highlights: Two rows of shops selling jewelry, silk, and souvenirs
Spectacular views of the Grand Canal from the bridge
Historic Rialto Market nearby with fresh fish and produce
tips: Visit early morning or late evening to avoid crowds. The market area is most active in the morning. Climb to the center of the bridge for the best Grand Canal photos. Shops on the bridge are tourist-oriented but atmospheric.
